Naming of the surah

• It is called Fatir, because it opens with this description of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which indicates the creation and originating of the great universe.

On the objectives of the surah

• Discussion of the signs of power and oneness, to establish that Allah alone deserves worship to the exclusion of others, the affirmation of resurrection, rising again, and recompense on the Day of Judgment, and the explanation of the inability of the creatures that the polytheists worship.

• Mention of the clear proofs of Allah's oneness, such as the variety of fruits in their colours and tastes, and the differences among mountains, people, animals and livestock in their kinds, forms and colours. All of them bear witness to the existence of Allah and speak of His greatness and majesty.

• Praise of the people of awe, purification and enlightened insight, who respond to the call of the Prophet (ﷺ), an explanation of the reward they have, and a warning to the deniers and a notice to them of the punishment prepared for them.

• An explanation of the great difference between the believer and the disbeliever, and between the righteous and the wicked, by way of the parables of the blind and the seeing, the darkness and the light, and the living and the dead.

[The Tafsir]

Praise of Allah with His attributes, all of which are attributes of perfection, and for His blessings, both apparent and hidden, religious and worldly; the Creator of the heavens and the earth and their Originator, who makes the angels messengers to whomever He wills of His servants, and in whatever He wills of His command and prohibition. Among the great power of Allah is that He made the angels possessors of wings, two, three and four, with which they fly, to carry out what Allah has commanded. He adds to His creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things Competent; nothing can resist Him.

Whatever Allah opens to people of provision, rain, health, knowledge, and other blessings, no one can withhold that mercy, and whatever He withholds of it, no one can release after Him, glorified and exalted is He. He is the Almighty, the Subduer of everything, the All-Wise who sends mercy and withholds it in accordance with His wisdom.

O people, remember the favour of Allah upon you, with your hearts, your tongues and your limbs. There is no creator for you other than Allah, who provides for you from the sky with rain, and from the earth with water, minerals and other things. There is no deity except Him, alone, with no partner. So how are you turned away from His oneness and worship?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 35, verse 4:

"And if your people deny you, O Messenger, then messengers before you were denied as well. And all matters will return to Allah in the Hereafter, and He will recompense each according to what he deserves. In this is consolation for the Messenger ﷺ."

O people, the promise of God regarding resurrection, reward, and punishment is a true and certain reality. So let not the worldly life, with its desires and aims, deceive you, and let not the Devil deceive you about God. Indeed, the Devil is an enemy to the children of Adam, so take him as an enemy and do not obey him. He only calls his followers to misguidance, so that they may become among the companions of the blazing Fire.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 35, verse 7:

Those who disbelieved in the fact that Allah alone is the true God, and disbelieved in what His messengers brought, will have a severe punishment in the Hereafter. As for those who believed in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and did righteous deeds, they will have forgiveness from their Lord, and He will overlook their sins after concealing them from others, and they will have a great reward, which is Paradise.

Is one whom Satan has made to see his evil deeds as good, [such as] disobedience to Allah, disbelief, and worship of other than Him among deities and idols, so that he regards them as fine and beautiful, [the same as one whom Allah has guided, so that he sees good as good and evil as evil]? Indeed, Allah leaves astray whomever He wills among His servants and guides whomever He wills. So do not let yourself perish in grief over the disbelief of these misguided people. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of their ugly deeds, and He will recompense them for them with the worst recompense.

And Allah is the One who sends the winds, so they stir up clouds. We drive the clouds to a barren land, so rain falls, and We bring the earth to life after its dryness, so it becomes green with vegetation. In the same way, Allah will bring the dead back to life on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 35, verse 10:

Whoever desires honour (ʿizzah), in this world or the Hereafter, let him seek it from Allah, for it is not attained except through obedience to Him. To Allah belongs all honour (al-ʿizzah jamīʿan). Whoever takes pride in the created, Allah will humble him, and whoever takes pride in the Creator, Allah will honour him. To Him, glorified is He, ascends the good word (dhikr), and righteous deeds raise it up. As for those who commit evil deeds, there is a severe punishment for them, and their scheming will perish and come to nothing, and it will not benefit them at all.

God created your father Adam from dust; then He made his offspring from a extract of lowly water (semen). Then He made you into males and females. No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge, and no one who is granted a long life is given extended life, nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is recorded in a Book with Him, namely the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), before she conceives him and before she gives birth to him. Indeed, Allah has enumerated all of that and known it before He created it. Nothing is added to what is decreed for him, nor is anything subtracted from it. Indeed, your creation, the knowledge of your circumstances, and their recording in the Preserved Tablet are easy and simple for Allah.

The two bodies of water are not alike: this one is sweet, very fresh, pleasant and easy to swallow, quenching thirst, and that one is salty, very bitter-salt. From both you eat fresh fish of delicious taste, and you extract adornment, namely pearls and coral, which you wear. You see ships in it cleaving through the waters, so that you may seek of His bounty, through trade and other means. In this is a sign of God's power and His oneness, and perhaps you will give thanks to God for these blessings with which He has favoured you.

And Allah causes the night to enter the day, so the day increases by the amount the night has decreased, and He causes the day to enter the night, so the night increases by the amount the day has decreased. He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. That is the One who did this: Allah, your Lord. To Him belongs all sovereignty. As for those you worship besides Allah, they do not possess even a qitmir (the thin white membrane that covers the date stone).

If you call upon them, O people, those deities besides God, they do not hear your call; and even if they were to hear, on the assumption, they would not answer you. On the Day of Resurrection they will disown your association with them. And none can inform you, O Messenger, more truthfully than God, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.

O people, you are in need of Allah in everything; you cannot dispense with Him even for the blink of an eye. He, glorified is He, is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghaniyy) above people and above all of His creation, the Praiseworthy (al-Hamid) in His essence, names and attributes, and the One who is praised for His blessings; for every blessment that people have is from Him, so to Him belong praise and thanks in every state.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 35, verse 16:

If Allah wills, He will destroy you, O people, and bring about another people who will obey Him and worship Him alone.
Destroying you and bringing a different creation in your place is not beyond Allah's power. Rather, that is easy and simple for Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 35, verse 18:

﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.﴾ And if a soul heavy with sins calls out for someone to carry some of its burden, none of it will be carried, even if the one it calls upon is a close relative, such as a father or a brother or the like. You, O Messenger, can only warn those who fear their Lord's punishment though they have not seen it, and who establish the prayer in its proper manner. Whoever purifies himself from polytheism and other sins, purifies himself only for his own benefit. To Allah, the Exalted, is the final return and destination of all creatures, and He will recompense each one according to what it deserves.

The blind and the seeing are not alike, nor are the darknesses and the light, nor the shade and the scorching heat, nor are the living and the dead alike. Indeed, God makes hear whomever He wills with a hearing of understanding and acceptance, but you, O Messenger, cannot make hear those in the graves. Just as the dead in their graves cannot be made to hear, so too these disbelievers cannot be made to hear, because their hearts are dead. You are only a warner to them of God's wrath and punishment.

We have sent you with the truth, which is faith in God and the laws of religion, as a bearer of good tidings of Paradise to whoever believes you and follows your guidance, and as a warner of the Fire to whoever denies you and disobeys you. There has not been a nation among the nations except that a warner came to it, warning it of the consequence of its disbelief and its misguidance.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 35, verse 26:

Then I seized those who disbelieved with various kinds of punishment. So see how was My rejection of their deeds and the descent of My punishment upon them?

Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We irrigate with it trees on the earth, and We bring forth from those trees fruits of varying colors: red, black, yellow, and other colors? And We created from the mountains tracts, white and red, of varying colors, and We created from the mountains peaks that are intensely black.

Here is the translation of the passage:

And We created from among mankind, beasts, camels, cattle and sheep of various colours likewise. Among them are the red, the white and the black, and other than these, just as the colours of fruits and mountains differ. Only those among His servants who have knowledge of Allah fear Him and guard against His punishment by obeying Him and abstaining from disobeying Him: those who know Him, His attributes, His law (shar') and His power over everything. Among these signs is the difference of these creatures despite the unity of their origin, and they reflect upon the admonitions and lessons contained in them. Indeed Allah is Almighty (ʿAzīz), Strong, not overcome; Forgiving (Ghafūr), who rewards those who obey Him and pardons them.

Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and act upon it, who establish the prayer at its appointed times, and who spend from what We have provided them, in obligatory and voluntary charities, secretly and openly: they hope through that for a commerce that will never slump and never perish, namely the pleasure of their Lord and attaining His abundant reward. This is so that Allah, exalted is He, may pay them the full reward of their deeds without any diminution, and increase for them the good deeds out of His bounty. Indeed Allah is Forgiving of their misdeeds, Appreciative of their good deeds, rewarding them for them with abundant reward.

And that which We have revealed to you, O Messenger, of the Qur'an is the truth, confirming the scriptures that Allah revealed to His messengers before you. Indeed Allah is All-Aware of the affairs of His servants, All-Seeing of their deeds, and He will recompense them for them.

Then, after the destruction of the earlier nations, We gave the Book to those whom We chose from the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ). Among them is one who wrongs himself by committing some of the sins; among them is one who is moderate (muqtasid), meaning one who performs the obligations and avoids the prohibitions; and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds (sabiq bil-khayrat) by Allah's permission, that is, one who hastens and strives in righteous deeds, both the obligatory and the voluntary. That giving of the Book and the choosing of this Ummah is the great bounty.

Gardens of perpetual dwelling, which they will enter, for those whom Allah has made heirs of the Book. Therein they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing there will be silk; that is, thin garments. And when they enter the Garden they will say: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us all sorrow. Indeed our Lord is Oft-Forgiving, for He has forgiven us our slips; Most Appreciative, for He has accepted from us the good deeds and multiplied them. It is He who, by His bounty, has settled us in the abode of the Garden; no fatigue touches us therein, nor does weariness."

Those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger will have the Fire of Hell, which is kindled. It will not be decreed for them to die so that they might die and find rest, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense everyone who persists in disbelief, who goes to extremes in it, who keeps on in it, and who insists upon it.

These unbelievers will cry out in the Fire of Hell from the intensity of the torment, pleading: "Our Lord, take us out of the Fire of Hell and send us back to the world, so that we may do righteous deeds different from what we used to do in our worldly life, and believe instead of disbelieving." He will say to them: "Did We not give you a sufficient span of life in this world, a lifetime long enough that whoever was going to take heed would have taken heed, and did the Prophet (ﷺ) not come to you? Yet you did not remember and did not take warning. So taste the torment of Hell. For the disbelievers there is no helper who can protect them from the punishment of Allah."

Indeed, Allah knows every unseen thing in the heavens and the earth, and indeed He is All-Knowing of the secrets of hearts. So fear Him, lest He discover you while you harbor doubt or polytheism concerning His oneness, or concerning the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), or that you disobey Him in matters less than that.

Allah is the One who made you, O people, successors on the earth, one generation succeeding another. So whoever among you denies the Oneness of Allah, his disbelief will harm himself. And the disbelief of the disbelievers adds nothing in their Lord's sight but abhorrence and wrath, and their disbelief in Allah adds nothing for them but misguidance and destruction.

Say, [O Messenger], to the polytheists: "Tell me: what have your partners created of the earth? Or do they have a share in the creation of the heavens with Allah? Or have We given them a Book so that they stand upon clear proof from it?" Rather, the disbelievers promise one another nothing but delusion and deception.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 35, verse 41:

Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease from their places. And if they were to cease from their places, none could hold them after Him. Indeed, Allah is Forbearing, delaying punishment from the disbelievers and the disobedient, and Forgiving toward whoever repents of his sin and turns back to Him.

The Quraysh disbelievers swore by Allah with the most emphatic oaths that, if a messenger from Allah came to them to warn them of Allah's punishment, they would surely be more upright and more inclined to follow the truth than the Jews and Christians and others. But when Muhammad (ﷺ) came to them, it only increased them in distance from the truth and in aversion to it.

Their oath was not made with a good intention or in search of the truth; rather, it is arrogance on earth toward creation. By it they intend evil scheming, deception, and falsehood. "But evil scheming does not encompass anyone except its own people." So do the arrogant schemers await anything but the punishment that befell those like them who came before them? "And you will not find any change in the way of Allah, nor will you find any alteration." No one is able to change or divert the punishment away from himself or from anyone else.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 35, verse 44:

Have not the disbelievers of Makkah travelled through the earth and looked at how the end of those before them was, such as ʿAad and Thamud and their like, and what destruction befell them, and how their dwellings became ruins when they denied the messengers? And were those disbelievers stronger in power and might than the disbelievers of Makkah? Yet Allah, exalted is He, is not one to be incapable of anything or to escape Him in anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed He is ever All-Knowing of their deeds, All-Powerful over their destruction.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 35, verse 45:

If Allah were to punish the people for the sins and disobedience they have committed, He would not leave upon the surface of the earth any creature that moves upon it. But He gives them respite and delays their punishment until a time known to Him. So when the time of their punishment comes, indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants: nothing of them is hidden from Him, and the knowledge of no matter of theirs escapes Him, and He will recompense them for what they have done of good or evil.
